literal: Attachment severed at-the-very-moment birth will-cut-off; otherwise impermanence to-see will-be.
translation: The very moment attachments are severed, the cycle of birth is cut off. Otherwise, one will only experience impermanence.
modern: பற்று நீங்கிய அப்பொழுதே பிறவித் துன்பம் அறுபடும்; இல்லையென்றால் நிலையற்ற தன்மையே காணப்படும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the direct result of true renunciation. The word 'பற்று' refers to worldly attachments or desires. When these attachments are completely severed ('அற்ற கண்ணே'), the cycle of birth ('பிறப்பு') is immediately cut off ('அறுக்கும்'). The word 'மற்று' means 'otherwise'—if attachments remain, one will only continue to experience the impermanence ('நிலையாமை') of worldly life. The emphatic 'ஏ' in 'கண்ணே' stresses that liberation happens at the exact moment of letting go.
